pages.text: Week two. The big machines are not single blocks but assemblies of $(thing)functional components$(), each with its own crafting chain. Like a real accelerator hall: nothing works alone.

The parts list reads like a CERN inventory: magnets, RF cavities, beam pipes, cryogenics, vacuum pumps, detectors, injectors, lenses, anchors, stabilisers and more. In reality, dipole magnets bend a beam, RF cavities kick it faster, and cryogenics keep superconductors below their critical temperature.

$(thing)Coils$() come in five tiers: Superconducting, Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium and Transfinite. Like a chain and its weakest link, a structure counts only its $(thing)lowest$() coil. Each tier above the first adds 25% speed, and some recipes need a minimum tier (JEI shows it).

$(thing)Field Emitters$() come in three tiers. The lowest emitter tier multiplies how many parallels the tuning panel allows.$(br2)The $(item)Structure Assembler$() places the best tier I carry; in creative, hold the tier you want in your off-hand. Mixing tiers works, but only the lowest counts - I checked twice.
Use on a multiblock controller to build every missing block from your inventory. Sneak-use to preview what is missing.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Spacetime Alloy Coil Block$(): Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block$(li)$(item)Graviton Field Emitter$(): Axiomatic Field Emitter, Chronal Field Projector, Dimensional Lift Projector, Empirical Notes I, Graviton Field Projector and more$(li)$(item)Dipole Bending Magnet$(): Antiproton Decelerator, Hyperion Synchrotron, Particle Spectrometer
